criterion: Average over 10 folds: each of self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) has at least 2 times the PFI of every other predictor, that is, a margin (PFI minus 2 x PFI of the other predictor) of at least 0 beyond Monte Carlo error in each of the 50 comparisons with other predictors; the lower bounds of their corrected 95% intervals are at least 0.0011 (the smallest relevant difference); a reversal counts only if the upper bound is at most -0.0011.
observation: self-rated health (A2) 0.0463 and depressed mood (D2) 0.0358 versus 0.0056 for M8, the largest other predictor (8.25 and 6.37 times); margin (PFI minus 2 x PFI of M8) 0.0351 [0.0280, 0.0422] and 0.0246 [0.0204, 0.0287]; weakest of the 50 comparisons with other predictors: depressed mood (D2) minus 2 x M8, 0.0246 [0.0204, 0.0287]. Against the largest other predictor of each fold, which can differ between folds: 0.0346 [0.0277, 0.0415] and 0.0241 [0.0201, 0.0281].
relevance: The learner average over refits on 10 training sets of 15,274 rows is the quantity the claim names; selected from this average, the estimates are optimistic (winner's curse).
summary: on average, self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) have 8.25 and 6.37 times the PFI of the largest other predictor, M8

property: Each of self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) matters relative to the accuracy of XGBoost.
criterion: Each of self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) has a mean PFI of at least 1% of the improvement of XGBoost over the model without predictors (0.0011 log-loss units), beyond Monte Carlo error; a shortfall counts only if the upper bound of the corrected interval is below it.
observation: self-rated health (A2) 0.0463 and depressed mood (D2) 0.0358 versus the minimum importance 0.0011 (1% of the improvement of 0.106, from 0.229 to 0.122).
relevance: Ratios and ranks are scale-free; the minimum importance excludes negligible predictors.
summary: self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) have 0.0463 and 0.0358, above the minimum importance 0.0011 (1% of the improvement)

property: The procedure computes the named quantity, and the wording is not broader than the scope.
criterion: Held-out marginal PFI as named in the scope; if grouped or conditional PFI reverses the result (beyond Monte Carlo error and the corrected interval), the wording names the marginal permutation.
observation: Held-out marginal PFI with log loss, 20 permutations per fold in 10 folds, as the scope names. No grouped or conditional comparison was requested.
relevance: Marginal permutation includes input combinations absent from the data; conditional and grouped PFI measure reliance on information a predictor does not share and on a group.
summary: held-out marginal PFI as the scope names; no grouped or conditional comparison was requested

property: The result recurs when XGBoost is refitted on other folds, with the selection repeated.
criterion: Selected anew in each fold, self-rated health (A2) and depressed mood (D2) are the two leading predictors with at least 2 times the PFI of every other predictor in at least 9 of 10 folds; a failing fold counts only beyond Monte Carlo error and by at least the smallest relevant difference (0.0011).
observation: Selected anew in each fold: 10 of 10 folds reproduce the result (cutoff 1: 0 of 10; cutoff 3: 1 of 10).
relevance: Refits on other folds and new permutations estimate the same learner PFI again; on the data that suggested the claim, this share remains optimistic.
summary: the result recurs in 10 of 10 folds
